title: Jesus, Lord, We Look to Thee
description: Jesus, Lord, We Look to Thee in Tonic Solfa to VIENNA, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 509.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Sevens (7.7.7.7), and this page sets them to VIENNA; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Je-sus, Lord, we look to thee, Let us in thy name a-gree; Show thy-self the Prince of peace; Bid our jars for ev-er cease.

lines: Jesus, Lord, we look to thee,
Let us in thy name agree;
Show thyself the Prince of peace;
Bid our jars for ever cease.
By thy reconciling love
Every stumbling-block remove;
Each to each unite, endear,
Come, and spread thy banner here!
Make us of one heart and mind,
Courteous, pitiful, and kind,
Lowly, meek, in thought and word?
Together like our Lord.
Let us for each other care,
Each the other's burden bear,
To thy church the pattern give,
Show how true believers live.
Free from anger and from pride,
Let us thus in God abide;
All the depths of love express,
All the heights of holiness!
Let us then with joy remove
To the family above;
On the wings of angels fly,
Show how true believers die.

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to VIENNA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
